name: Hydrogen
funFact: Hydrogen makes up about 75% of the visible universe's ordinary matter.

name: Helium
funFact: Helium was discovered in the Sun's spectrum before it was ever found on Earth.

name: Lithium
funFact: Lithium is light enough to float on water, and it powers many of our batteries.

name: Beryllium
funFact: Beryllium salts taste sweet, but the metal is highly toxic.

name: Boron
discoveredBy: Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac & Louis Jacques ThÃ©nard
funFact: Boron is essential for plants and gives borosilicate glass its heat resistance.

name: Carbon
funFact: Carbon forms more compounds than any other element and is the backbone of all known life.

name: Nitrogen
funFact: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.

name: Oxygen
funFact: Oxygen makes up about 21% of the air we breathe and is the most abundant element in Earth's crust.

name: Fluorine
funFact: Fluorine is the most electronegative element and can react with some noble gases.

name: Neon
funFact: Neon glows orange-red in discharge tubes; many neon signs actually use other gases too.

name: Sodium
funFact: Sodium is a soft metal that reacts violently with water and is half of table salt.

name: Magnesium
funFact: Magnesium burns with a brilliant white light and sits at the heart of chlorophyll.

name: Aluminium
funFact: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in Earth's crust, yet it was once more precious than gold.

name: Silicon
funFact: Silicon is the backbone of computer chips and the second most abundant element in Earth's crust.

name: Phosphorus
funFact: White phosphorus glows in the dark, which is where the word phosphorescence comes from.

name: Sulfur
funFact: Sulfur forms bright yellow crystals and smells of rotten eggs when bonded to hydrogen.

name: Chlorine
funFact: Chlorine is a greenish gas used to disinfect water and is the other half of table salt.

name: Argon
funFact: Argon is the most abundant noble gas in the atmosphere, making up about 0.93% of it.

name: Potassium
funFact: Potassium is essential for nerve and muscle function, which is why bananas are famous for it.

name: Calcium
funFact: Calcium builds bones and teeth, and gives limestone and chalk their structure.

name: Scandium
funFact: Scandium is used in lightweight bicycle frames and high-intensity stadium lamps.

name: Titanium
funFact: Titanium is as strong as steel but about 45% lighter, and it resists corrosion beautifully.

name: Vanadium
funFact: Vanadium forms beautifully colored compounds and is named after the Norse goddess Vanadis.

name: Chromium
funFact: Chromium gives rubies their red and emeralds their green, and makes stainless steel stainless.

name: Manganese
funFact: Manganese is essential for steelmaking and for oxygen production in plants.

name: Iron
funFact: Earth's core is mostly iron, and its movement generates our planet's magnetic field.

name: Cobalt
funFact: Cobalt gives cobalt-blue glass its rich color and is essential in many batteries.

name: Nickel
funFact: Nickel is magnetic, takes a high polish, and appears in coins and superalloys.

name: Copper
funFact: Copper was one of the first metals ever used, and it kills microbes on contact.

name: Zinc
funFact: Zinc protects steel from rust through galvanization and is essential for human immunity.

name: Gallium
funFact: Gallium melts in your hand at about 30°C, making it a wonderfully playful metal.

name: Germanium
funFact: Germanium powered the first transistor before silicon took over.

name: Arsenic
funFact: Arsenic was once called inheritance powder; today it is used in semiconductors.

name: Selenium
funFact: Selenium is named after the Moon, glows in the dark, and supports human metabolism.

name: Bromine
funFact: Bromine is one of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature.

name: Krypton
funFact: Krypton once helped define the length of the meter and gives some lights a white glow.

name: Rubidium
funFact: Rubidium is so reactive that it ignites in air, and its atoms are used in atomic clocks.

name: Strontium
funFact: Strontium gives fireworks their brilliant red color.

name: Yttrium
funFact: Yttrium was found in lunar samples brought back by Apollo 11 and is used in LED phosphors.

name: Zirconium
funFact: Zirconium is highly corrosion-resistant and is used in nuclear reactors.

name: Niobium
funFact: Superconducting niobium magnets power MRI machines and particle colliders.

name: Molybdenum
funFact: Molybdenum strengthens steel and works as a high-temperature lubricant.

name: Technetium
funFact: Technetium was the first artificially produced element and is used in medical imaging.

name: Ruthenium
funFact: Ruthenium is named after Russia and is used in electronics and solar technologies.

name: Rhodium
funFact: Rhodium is one of the rarest precious metals and is found in catalytic converters.

name: Palladium
funFact: Palladium can absorb up to 900 times its own volume of hydrogen.

name: Silver
funFact: Silver is the best electrical and thermal conductor of all the elements.

name: Cadmium
discoveredBy: Karl Samuel Leberecht Hermann & Friedrich Stromeyer
funFact: Cadmium is highly toxic, but it once gave us bright yellow pigments and rechargeable batteries.

name: Indium
funFact: Indium makes touchscreens work as a transparent conductive oxide.

name: Tin
funFact: Bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, powered an entire age of human history.

name: Antimony
funFact: Ancient Egyptians used antimony compounds as eyeliner.

name: Tellurium
funFact: Tellurium is rarer than platinum in Earth's crust and is used in solar panels.

name: Iodine
funFact: Iodine is essential for the thyroid and sublimes into a beautiful violet vapor.

name: Xenon
funFact: Xenon powers ion thrusters on spacecraft and can form compounds with fluorine.

name: Caesium
funFact: Caesium is the most reactive metal, and its atomic clock defines the second.

name: Barium
funFact: A barium meal makes the digestive tract visible in X-rays.

name: Lanthanum
funFact: Lanthanum is used in camera lenses and hybrid car batteries.

name: Cerium
funFact: Cerium is the most abundant rare-earth element and helps clean up vehicle exhaust.

name: Praseodymium
funFact: Praseodymium colors glass green and gives welder's goggles their protective tint.

name: Neodymium
funFact: Neodymium magnets are the strongest permanent magnets ever made.

name: Promethium
discoveredBy: Jacob A. Marinsky, Lawrence E. Glendenin & Charles D. Coryell
funFact: Promethium is the only rare-earth element with no stable isotopes.

name: Samarium
funFact: Samarium-cobalt magnets hold their magnetism at extreme temperatures.

name: Europium
funFact: Europium gives television screens and banknotes their red glow under ultraviolet light.

name: Gadolinium
funFact: Gadolinium is highly magnetic and is used as an MRI contrast agent.

name: Terbium
funFact: Terbium gives green phosphors to screens and fluorescent lamps.

name: Dysprosium
funFact: Dysprosium keeps neodymium magnets working at the high temperatures inside electric motors.

name: Holmium
funFact: Holmium has one of the strongest magnetic moments of any element and is used in lasers.

name: Erbium
funFact: Erbium-doped fiber amplifiers make long-distance internet connections possible.

name: Thulium
funFact: Thulium is one of the rarest lanthanides and is used in portable X-ray machines.

name: Ytterbium
funFact: Ytterbium is used in some of the most accurate optical atomic clocks ever built.

name: Lutetium
discoveredBy: Georges Urbain & Carl Auer von Welsbach
funFact: Lutetium is the densest and hardest lanthanide and is used in PET scanners.

name: Hafnium
funFact: Hafnium controls nuclear reactions in control rods and insulates modern computer chips.

name: Tantalum
funFact: Tantalum is highly corrosion-resistant and is used in capacitors and surgical implants.

name: Tungsten
funFact: Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal, at 3,422°C.

name: Rhenium
discoveredBy: Walter Noddack, Ida Tacke & Otto Berg
funFact: Rhenium was the last stable element to be discovered and is used in jet engine alloys.

name: Osmium
funFact: Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element, about twice as dense as lead.

name: Iridium
funFact: Iridium is more corrosion-resistant than gold and is abundant in the layer marking the dinosaurs' extinction.

name: Platinum
funFact: Platinum is so unreactive that it is used in jewelry, catalytic converters, and chemotherapy.

name: Gold
funFact: Gold is forged in neutron-star collisions and is both chemically inert and highly conductive.

name: Mercury
funFact: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

name: Thallium
funFact: Thallium is extremely toxic and odorless, and was once used as a rat poison.

name: Lead
funFact: Lead is dense and malleable, but its toxicity led to its removal from pipes and paint.

name: Bismuth
funFact: Bismuth forms striking iridescent crystal staircases and is far less toxic than lead.

name: Polonium
funFact: Polonium was discovered by Marie Curie and named after her homeland, Poland.

name: Astatine
discoveredBy: Dale R. Corson, Kenneth R. MacKenzie & Emilio SegrÃ¨
funFact: Astatine is the rarest naturally occurring element, with less than 30 grams in Earth's crust at any time.

name: Radon
funFact: Radon is a radioactive gas that seeps from rocks and is a leading cause of lung cancer.

name: Francium
funFact: Francium is the least stable naturally occurring element, with only a few grams existing at once.

name: Radium
funFact: Radium glows faintly blue and was once used to paint luminous watch dials.

name: Actinium
funFact: Actinium glows blue in the dark and is used in targeted cancer treatments.

name: Thorium
funFact: Thorium is about three times more abundant than uranium and is a potential nuclear fuel.

name: Protactinium
funFact: Protactinium is one of the rarest and most expensive naturally occurring elements.

name: Uranium
funFact: Uranium is the heaviest primordial element, and its 235 isotope fuels nuclear reactors.

name: Neptunium
funFact: Neptunium was the first transuranium element to be discovered and is named after Neptune.

name: Plutonium
funFact: A small plutonium pellet powers spacecraft such as Voyager and Perseverance.

name: Americium
funFact: A tiny amount of americium in smoke detectors ionizes the air to sense smoke.

name: Curium
funFact: Curium is named after the Curies and has been used in Mars rover spectrometers.

name: Berkelium
funFact: Berkelium is named after Berkeley, California, and is used to create even heavier elements.

name: Californium
funFact: Californium is a powerful neutron source used to start nuclear reactors.

name: Einsteinium
funFact: Einsteinium was discovered in the fallout of the first hydrogen bomb test, Ivy Mike.

name: Fermium
funFact: Fermium was also discovered in Ivy Mike debris and is named after Enrico Fermi.

name: Mendelevium
funFact: Mendelevium is named after Dmitri Mendeleev, the creator of the periodic table.

name: Nobelium
funFact: Nobelium is named after Alfred Nobel, and only a few atoms have ever been made.

name: Lawrencium
funFact: Lawrencium is named after Ernest Lawrence, the inventor of the cyclotron.

name: Rutherfordium
funFact: Rutherfordium is named after Ernest Rutherford, the father of nuclear physics.

name: Dubnium
funFact: Dubnium is named after Dubna, Russia, home of the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research.

name: Seaborgium
funFact: Seaborgium was named after Glenn Seaborg while he was still alive, a rare honor.

name: Bohrium
funFact: Bohrium is named after Niels Bohr, who developed the modern model of the atom.

name: Hassium
funFact: Hassium is named after Hesse, Germany, and may be the densest element ever made.

name: Meitnerium
funFact: Meitnerium is named after Lise Meitner, who helped explain nuclear fission.

name: Darmstadtium
funFact: Darmstadtium was created atom by atom in Darmstadt, Germany.

name: Roentgenium
funFact: Roentgenium is named after Wilhelm RÃ¶ntgen, the discoverer of X-rays.

name: Copernicium
funFact: Copernicium is named after Nicolaus Copernicus, who put the Sun at the center of the solar system.

name: Nihonium
funFact: Nihonium is named after Japan, and was the first element discovered in Asia.

name: Flerovium
funFact: Flerovium is named after the Flerov Laboratory, and its properties are still mostly predicted.

name: Moscovium
funFact: Moscovium is named after the Moscow region, where it was synthesized.

name: Livermorium
funFact: Livermorium is named after the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

name: Tennessine
funFact: Tennessine is named after Tennessee, home to Oak Ridge and Vanderbilt researchers.

name: Oganesson
funFact: Oganesson is named after Yuri Oganessian, a living pioneer of superheavy elements.
